literature_notes: All three ledger lines were evaluated. L1 reports a C-terminal 3xHA tag on full-length human FOLR1 in HEK293T cells; FOLR1 is a GPI-anchored protein whose GPI signal/propeptide (approximately residues 234–257) is cleaved by GPI transamidase at the omega site (~S233). A tag appended after residue 257 is removed with the propeptide during GPI processing — a silent failure analogous to placing a tag upstream of a signal peptide — and the ledger clip confirms only western-blot detection, not cell-surface display. L2 reports a C-terminal GFP fusion on C. elegans FOLR-1 (an ortholog); the same GPI-propeptide cleavage concern applies, and no surface localisation is confirmed. L3 reports a Myc-tagged FOLR1 construct in K562 cells but states no tag position, disqualifying it under the rule that a construct whose tag position is unstated cannot be pinned. No ledger line supports a validated or topology-derived extracellular surface tag site for human FOLR1.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal 3xHA tag appended after the last residue of the GPI propeptide; the propeptide (~234–257) is cleaved by GPI transamidase during processing, so the tag is removed with the propeptide and does not reach the cell surface.
